Malate, Manila, Philippines 1004 Dear Mr. David: This is in reference to your letter dated 25 April 2017 seeking for clarification on Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG)-Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 2017-1 dated 22 February 2017 re: "Updated Guidelines on the Appropriation and Utilization of the Twenty Percent (20%) of the Annual Internal Revenue Allotment (IRA) for Development Projects. " In your query, you cited the provisions of DILG-DBM JMC No. 2011-11 saying that they are neither amended nor explicitly stated, to wit: "I. Projects chargeable against the 20% DF under Social Development (Section 3): a. Purchase or repair of area-wide calamity related alarm or warning system; and b. Purchase or repair of appropriate calamity related rescue operations equipment such as inflatable boats, breathing apparatus, extraction tools, safe line rescue ropes, fire extinguishers, chainsaws, two (2) way handheld radios and the like. 2. Construction, repair, refinishing of administrative offices", an item not eligible Tor funding under the 20% DF (Section 4). " Amending DILG-DBM Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1, dated September 20, 2005, entitled, "Guidelines on the Appropriation and Utilization of the 20% of the Annual Internal revenue Allotment for Development Projects" and DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2010-138 dated December 2, 2010, entitled "Use of the 20% Component of the Annual Internal Revenue Allotment Shares

You also added in your letter that Section 8 (Repealing Clause) of JMC No. 2017-1 states that "all existing issuances of' the DILG or the DBM, which are not consistent with this newly issued JIVIC are superseded accordingly" may mean that the above-stated specific provisions covered under the previous JMC No. 2011-I dated 13 April 2011 may still be interpreted as valid since they are not inconsistent with the new JMC." This Department will answer your queries in the following discussions: Projects chargeable against the 20% Development Fund (DF) under Social Development As you pointed out, Items 3.1.5 and 3.1.7 of the JMC No. 2011-1 were not anymore included in the enumeration of the JMC No. 2017-1. However, these two items refer specifically to calamity-related purchases sourced out from the 20% DF in JMC No. 2011-1. It is this Department's view that the exclusion of these items in the new JMC is intended because the said purchases are also covered by the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) of the LGU. Relative thereto is the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC), DBM and DILG JMC No. 2013-12 dated 25 March 2013 which allows the procurement/acquisition of disaster equipment for disaster response and rescue activities from the 70% of LDRRMF. The said JMC specifically provides: "5.5.1 The seventy percent (70%) of the LDRRMF, which is intended for disaster prevention and mitigation, preparedness, response, rehabilitation and recovery, may also be utilized to procure early warning systems, preparedness equipment and other equipage for floods, earthquake, volcanic eruptions, landslide and other natural and man-made calamities. 55.2 The purchase or received from donations and used solely for disaster response and rescue activities shall be classified as "Disaster Response and Rescue Equipment Ex. Inflatable boats, Megaphones including Sirens and Portable Generator Set. 5.5.3 The acquisition of heavy equipment although used in disaster and rescue activities shall be classified under response the account "Construction and Heavy Equipment". 2 Allocation and Utilization of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF)

Ex. Dump Trucks, Forklift, Backhoe and Grader 5.5.4 On the other hand, the purchase/acquisition of expandable items such as fire extinguisher, flood light, chainsaw, ax, ropes, ladder, breathing apparatus, flashlight and the like shall be classified as "Supplies or Inventories. " As gleaned from the above-cited provisions of the NDRRMC-DBM-DILG JMC No. 2013-1, it can be concluded that Items 3.1.5 and 3.1.7 of JMC No. 2011-1 were explicitly excluded in the recent JMC in view of the fact that the purchase of said equipment can be sourced-out from the 70% of LDDRMF, and Supplies and Inventories of the LGU. Construction, repair, refinishing of administrative offices It was observed that the "Construction, repair or refinishing of administrative offices" which was specifically enumerated in "Expenditure Items Not Covered (Item 4.0)" under DILG-DBM JMC No. 2011-I was not anymore included in the list under Item 4.0 of DILG- DBM JMC No. 2017-1. The exclusion of the said provision in the Item 4.0 can be traced in 2013 wherein after the typhoon Yolanda, this Department received requests for exemption from JMC No. 2011-1 in order for the LGUs to repair their administrative offices. A joint issuance between the Department and the DBM was crafted to exempt from this provision of the JMC the LGUs declared under State of Calamity. Hence, it is this Department's view that the construction, repair, refinishing of administrative offices was intentionally removed from Item 4.0 in order for the LGUs to have additional funding for the construction of their administrative offices which is necessary for the development of every LGU. However, it must be noted that the purchase of administrative office' fixtures, equipment or appliances is still covered by Item 4.0 or it cannot be bought out Of the 20% DF of the LGU. DILG-DBAIJMC' No. 2017-1 repealed (by implication) JMCNO. 2011-1 In sum, JMC No. 2017-1 provides for the revised lists of what can and cannot be funded by the 20% DF of the LGU. The repealing clause of the new JMC provides: "AI/ issuances by the DILG or the DBM which are not consistent herewith are hereby superseded accordingly. Any future issuance(s) of either the DBM or the DILG in relation to the appropriation and utilization of the 20% DIR shall be made in accordance with this JMC. " It can be argued that the repeal of JMC No. 2011-1 was not expressly stated in the repealing clause of the new JMC. However, our jurisdiction recognized the repeal by

(7 implication, and the herein situation falls squarely under the second category of repeal by implication, to wit: There are two categories OT repeal by implication. The first is where provisions in the two acts on the same subject matter are in an irreconcilable conflict, [he later act to the extent of the conflict constitutes an implied repeal of' the earlier one. The second is if the later act covers the whole subject of the earlier one and is clearly intended as a substitute, it will operate to repeal the earlier law.3(Emphasis ours) Hence, JMC No. 2017-01 is clearly intended as substitute of JMC No. 2011-1. Thus, it is JMC No. 2017-1 entitled "Updated Guidelines on the Appropriation and Utilization of the Twenty Percent (20%) of' the Annual Internal Revenue Allotment (IRA) for Development Projects" should be the basis of the LGUs for utilization of their 20% Development Fund. We hope we had addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORI THE SECRETARY: AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary Copy furnished: - OUSLG 201 - Asec. Ester A.
